title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Incretin Therapies: Recent FDA and EMA Approvals and the Clinical Pipeline
summary: Recent FDA and EMA approvals of GLP-1 and incretin therapies, including oral orforglipron and semaglutide, plus the late-stage multi-agonist clinical pipeline.
body_markdown:
## GLP-1 receptor agonists and incretin therapies: recent FDA and EMA decisions and the clinical pipeline (September 2026)


### Key takeaways


- **Orforglipron is now approved by FDA.** FDA approved FOUNDAYO (orforglipron) tablets under NDA 220934 on April 1, 2026, as a Type 1 new molecular entity[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=209)[655](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=655) . It was reviewed under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot and approved 50 days after filing, the first new molecular entity approved under that program (FDA press release, April 1, 2026). It is the first small-molecule, non-peptide oral GLP-1 receptor agonist approved by FDA, and it carries no food or water dosing restrictions[1171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1171)[665](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=665) . No EMA EPAR for orforglipron was found as of this review.
- **Oral semaglutide for obesity came first in the US.** FDA approved oral Wegovy (semaglutide 25 mg tablets) under NDA 218316 on December 22, 2025[1015](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1015)[480](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=480) . The EU added Wegovy tablets as an extension of the existing marketing authorisation[651](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=651) .
- **Established incretins keep adding indications and doses.** Examples are Wegovy HD 7.2 mg (FDA, March 19, 2026)[1213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1213) , the Wegovy MASH accelerated approval (August 15, 2025)[744](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=744) , and a cardiovascular risk-reduction indication for Mounjaro in type 2 diabetes (August 27, 2026)[961](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=961) . In the EU, the recent actions were Kayshild (semaglutide for MASH, March 26, 2026)[904](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=904) , Kyinsu (insulin icodec/semaglutide, November 24, 2025)[707](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=707) , and the first hybrid liraglutide products referencing Saxenda (July 2026)[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=300)[604](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=604) .
- **The late-stage pipeline has moved past single-agonist GLP-1.** ClinicalTrials.gov shows large Phase 3 programs for retatrutide, CagriSema, maridebart cafraglutide, survodutide, NNC0487-0111, zenagamtide, eloralintide, VK2735 and AZD6234. Behind them is a broad group of Chinese and other ex-US GLP-1-based candidates, many of them oral.


---


### 1. Orforglipron (FOUNDAYO): the first approved non-peptide oral GLP-1 receptor agonist


#### Regulatory record


Item Detail


Application NDA 220934, Eli Lilly and Co; ORIG, submission class Type 1 (NME)[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=209) ; CNPV pilot, approved 50 days after filing


Approval date April 1, 2026[655](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=655)[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=219)


Latest action Labeling supplement approved August 4, 2026[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=206)[663](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=663)


Molecule Selective, orally administered small-molecule, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist, supplied as the calcium salt in film-coated tablets[1171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1171)[1177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1177)


Pharmacology Activates the human GLP-1 receptor (cAMP signalling). No activity at glucagon, GIP or GLP-2 receptors. Signalling biased toward cAMP over beta-arrestin recruitment[1167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1167)[1171](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1171)


#### Indication and dosing


FOUNDAYO is indicated, together with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, "to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term" in adults with obesity, or in adults with overweight and at least one weight-related comorbid condition[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659) . Concomitant use with another GLP-1 receptor agonist is not recommended[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659) .


- Tablet strengths are 0.8, 2.5, 5.5, 9, 14.5 and 17.2 mg, taken once daily. Treatment starts at 0.8 mg, and each step up follows at least 30 days on the current dose, to a maximum of 17.2 mg[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659) .
- It may be taken with or without food. FDA's review describes the product as having a "lack of food and water dosing restrictions"[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659)[665](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=665) . The US-approved oral semaglutide products do not share this feature.
- The label contains CYP3A4 interaction limits. The maximum dose is 9 mg with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors that also inhibit OATP1B, and strong CYP3A4 inducers, should be avoided[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659) .


#### Pivotal evidence


FDA based substantial evidence of effectiveness on two 72-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials[922](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=922)[935](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=935) :


Trial Population Placebo-adjusted weight change at Week 72 (trial doses 6 / 12 / 36 mg, labeled as FOUNDAYO 5.5 / 9 / 17.2 mg)


ATTAIN-1 (NCT05869903), N=3,127 Obesity, or overweight with a comorbidity, without T2D −5.3% / −6.2% / −9.0%, all p<0.001[939](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=939)


ATTAIN-2 (NCT05872620), N=1,613 BMI ≥27 kg/m² with T2D (HbA1c 7% to 10%) −2.6% / −4.5% / −7.1%, all p<0.001[921](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=921)


FDA's clinical interpretation depended on the population. In ATTAIN-1, all three doses met the 5% threshold for clinically meaningful placebo-adjusted weight loss. In ATTAIN-2, only 36 mg clearly met it. FDA judged 12 mg borderline and found that 6 mg did not meet the threshold[926](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=926)[927](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=927) . The overall benefit-risk assessment was favorable[933](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=933)[658](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=658) .


#### Safety and postmarketing obligations


- **Boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors.** FDA applied the boxed warning even though orforglipron is not pharmacologically active in rats or mice and did not cause tumors in rodent studies. FDA treats C-cell findings as an on-target GLP-1 receptor class effect whose human relevance is unknown[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659)[864](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=864)[875](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=875) .
- **Gastrointestinal tolerability.** In the pooled pivotal trials, GI adverse events occurred in about 66% of orforglipron patients versus 37% on placebo. Discontinuations due to adverse events were 8.1% versus 3.5%[933](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=933) . The label restarts titration at a lower dose after 7 or more missed doses[870](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=870) .
- **Hepatic.** FDA found no substantial evidence of increased idiosyncratic liver-injury risk[933](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=933) . It nonetheless requested 5 years of enhanced pharmacovigilance, with serious DILI cases (jaundice, liver failure, transplant, death) submitted as 15-day Alert reports[881](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=881) . This is a small-molecule-specific obligation not seen with the peptide agonists.
- **505(o) PMRs.** The PMRs include a class-wide medullary thyroid carcinoma registry case series running at least 15 years[863](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=863)[864](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=864) and a pediatric obesity registry cohort study of at least 10 years (PMR 4977-3)[882](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=882) . FDA also identified pregnancy exposure as a risk requiring further assessment[882](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=882) .
- **No REMS** was required[863](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=863) .


#### What the orforglipron trial registry signals next


The ClinicalTrials.gov portfolio suggests Lilly is building toward label expansion well beyond chronic weight management:


- **Type 2 diabetes (ACHIEVE program).** ACHIEVE-1 (completed)[29](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05971940) , ACHIEVE-2 versus dapagliflozin[27](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06192108) , ACHIEVE-3 versus semaglutide[21](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06045221) , ACHIEVE-4 versus insulin glargine[23](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05803421) , ACHIEVE-5[30](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06109311) , ACHIEVE-J long-term safety (completed)[19](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06010004) , ACHIEVE-RAM in Ramadan fasting[15](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07613307) , and ACHIEVE-PEDS versus dulaglutide in pediatric T2D[9](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07668336) . The approved label is limited to weight reduction[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659) , so a T2D indication remains a prospective filing.
- **Obesity comorbidities and outcomes.** A cardiovascular outcomes trial in ASCVD[24](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07241390) , peripheral artery disease (ATTAIN-PAD)[41](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07223593) , obstructive sleep apnea (ATTAIN-OSA)[49](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06649045) , hypertension master protocols[10](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06952530)[11](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06948435)[16](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06948422) , knee osteoarthritis pain[13](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07153471) , stress urinary incontinence[47](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07202884) , and weight-maintenance after prior therapy[48](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06584916) .
- **Special populations and regions.** Adolescents[8](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06672939) , Japan (ATTAIN-J)[6](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05931380) , China (ATTAIN-CN)[17](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07790861) , and overweight individuals at risk of obesity complications (ATTAIN-NOW)[45](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07794579) .

### 2. Other recent FDA actions in the incretin class


Date Product (application) Action


Aug 27, 2026 Mounjaro (NDA 215866, S-044/S-045) New indication to reduce MACE risk in adults with T2D at high CV risk (SURPASS-CVOT). Updated diabetic retinopathy warning. 2.5 mg may now be used for ongoing glycemic control[961](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=961)


Aug 26, 2026 Zepbound (NDA 217806, S-041) No new indication. Recent Major Change to Warnings and Precautions 5.8 (diabetic retinopathy complications in T2D), based on SURPASS-CVOT[1187](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1187)[1184](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1184)


Mar 19, 2026 Wegovy HD (NDA 215256, S-029) 7.2 mg once weekly for adults who tolerated 2.4 mg for at least 4 weeks and need additional weight reduction[1213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1213)[1223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1223)


Dec 22, 2025 Wegovy tablets (NDA 218316, ORIG, Type 3) Oral semaglutide 25 mg once daily for chronic weight management and MACE risk reduction in adults with established CVD and obesity or overweight[1015](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1015)[1017](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1017)[1032](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1032)


Aug 15, 2025 Wegovy (NDA 215256, S-024, priority) Accelerated approval for noncirrhotic MASH with F2 to F3 fibrosis[744](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=744)


The oral Wegovy review shows how far FDA would bridge. OASIS 4 (64 weeks, placebo-controlled) was the only pivotal adequate and well-controlled trial[1032](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1032)[1036](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1036) . The cardiovascular indication was extended to the tablet by pharmacokinetic bridging to the subcutaneous SELECT trial, without a dedicated outcomes trial[1033](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1033) .


Class-wide labeling activity also continues. The Drugs@FDA record shows coordinated labeling supplements across GLP-1 products (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Victoza, Saxenda, Trulicity, Byetta, Bydureon, Adlyxin, Soliqua, Xultophy) on shared action dates in November 2024, May 2025 and October 2025[477](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=477)[483](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=483)[486](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=486)[495](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=495)[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=504)[506](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=506)[513](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=513)[522](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=522)[472](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=472)[531](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=531) .

### 3. Recent EMA decisions


EU authorisation Product Summary


15 Jul 2026 Ablymico and Liraglutide STADA (liraglutide, STADA) Article 10(3) hybrid applications with Saxenda as reference product. The hybrid route was used because the pro-peptide is chemically produced while the reference is biologically derived. Bioequivalence to Saxenda was shown. Indicated for weight management[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=300)[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=339)[604](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=604)[607](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=607)[613](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=613)


26 Mar 2026 Kayshild (semaglutide, Novo Nordisk) Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide, titrated to 2.4 mg, for non-cirrhotic MASH with F2 to F3 fibrosis[904](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=904)[906](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=906)[919](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=919)


24 Nov 2025 Kyinsu (insulin icodec/semaglutide, Novo Nordisk) Once-weekly fixed-ratio combination for adults with T2D insufficiently controlled on basal insulin or GLP-1 RAs[707](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=707)[720](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=720)


Extension Wegovy (semaglutide) New 7.2 mg once-weekly maintenance dose for adults with BMI ≥30 kg/m² at initiation[636](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=636) . Wegovy tablets 1.5, 4, 9 and 25 mg added via line extension[651](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=651)


#### Where EMA and FDA diverge


- **Cardiovascular claims.** CHMP did not grant Wegovy a separate MACE-reduction indication. SELECT results were placed in SmPC section 5.1 and cross-referenced from the weight-management indication[637](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=637) . For the tablets, EMA concluded that cardiovascular benefit could not be assumed from subcutaneous data and removed the section 4.1 cardiovascular reference[639](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=639) . FDA took the opposite position and granted the tablet a MACE indication by PK bridging[1033](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1033) .
- **Comorbidity indications.** For Mounjaro, CHMP concluded that a standalone OSA indication was unnecessary because the population is already covered by the weight-management indication. SURMOUNT-OSA data went into SmPC sections 4.1, 4.8 and 5.1 instead[897](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=897)[889](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=889)[884](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=884) .
- **Pediatric scope.** Mounjaro's EU T2D indication extends to children aged 10 years and older[884](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=884) .


For sponsors, this means EU labeling strategy for new incretins should plan on comorbidity and outcomes data appearing in section 5.1 rather than as discrete indications.


No EPARs were found for orforglipron, cagrilintide/CagriSema, survodutide or retatrutide as of this review.

#### Patterns across the registry


1. **Head-to-head designs against approved incretins are now common.** Examples are retatrutide versus tirzepatide[689](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06662383) , CagriSema versus tirzepatide[997](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06131437) , zenagamtide versus semaglutide[71](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07668414) , NNC0487-0111 versus semaglutide[94](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07400107) , KAI-9531 versus semaglutide[83](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07284979) , and GZR18 versus Wegovy[91](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07150975) . This reflects an active-comparator environment in which placebo-only data may not be enough for payers or for differentiation claims.
2. **Outcomes and comorbidity trials start alongside registration trials.** CV outcomes trials are registered for orforglipron[24](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07241390) , retatrutide[697](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06383390) , maridebart cafraglutide[99](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07037433) and survodutide[74](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06077864) . HFpEF, OSA, MASH, CKD and osteoarthritis are repeated targets[101](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07037459)[858](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07225686)[734](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06632444)[692](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07035093)[784](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07353931) .
3. **Amylin-based agents are the next competitive tier.** Candidates include CagriSema, NNC0487-0111, eloralintide, and petrelintide combined with enicepatide (ZYNERGY)[147](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07589686) . Lilly is also combining eloralintide with macupatide[140](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07215559) and with tirzepatide[777](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06916065) . AstraZeneca's SELENE 3 tests AZD6234 as an adjunct to existing incretin therapy[80](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07776509) .
4. **More oral candidates are following orforglipron.** Beyond oral Wegovy and FOUNDAYO, the registry lists zenagamtide tablets[69](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07720271) , oral NNC0487-0111[1284](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06542874) , oral VK2735[1196](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06828055) , and weekly oral ecnoglutide (EVOLVE-2)[145](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07281937) . Other oral candidates are once-daily RGT001-075 (COMO-1)[138](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06867718) , BGM0504 tablets[176](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07658560) , MWN109 tablets[182](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07791524) , CX11 tablets[167](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07011797) , DA-302168S tablets[163](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06953063) , and a GZR18 tablet in Phase 1[670](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06554054) .
5. **Chinese sponsors are a substantial share of the pipeline.** Phase 3 programs include VCT220[60](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06939296) , HDM1005[86](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07279194) , BGM0504[90](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06704581) , RAY1225[93](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06893016) , MWN109[109](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07778693) , MDR-001[92](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07274137) , UBT251 (OSA)[97](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07767942) and ecnoglutide[980](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07836270)[985](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07734311) . Semaglutide copies from CSPC and Jiuyuan are in comparative Phase 3 trials against Wegovy[96](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06604624)[95](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06633783) . Mazdutide, a dual GLP-1R/GCGR agonist[804](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07824895) , appears in the registry mainly in investigator-initiated Phase 4 studies in China[763](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07654062)[766](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07657676) , which indicates post-approval use in that market.
6. **Mechanism transparency varies.** Several sponsors, notably for retatrutide, survodutide, maridebart cafraglutide, eloralintide and AZD6234, do not state receptor targets in the retrieved registry records. RA teams building competitive landscapes should confirm mechanism from FDA or EMA documents or peer-reviewed sources, not from CT.gov alone.

### 5. Regulatory considerations for sponsors


- **Small-molecule GLP-1 RAs bring a different safety review focus.** For orforglipron, FDA added hepatic enhanced pharmacovigilance[881](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=881) and CYP3A4/OATP1B dose limits[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659) on top of the class-wide boxed warning and MTC registry PMR[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=659)[863](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=863) . Sponsors of other non-peptide oral agents should expect the same DILI and DDI scrutiny.
- **The class-wide PMR package now applies by default.** New entrants should budget for a 15-year MTC registry and a pediatric obesity registry[863](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=863)[882](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=882) .
- **FDA and EMA handle outcomes claims differently.** FDA grants discrete MACE indications and accepts PK bridging across formulations[1033](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=1033)[961](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=961) . CHMP tends to place outcomes data in SmPC section 5.1 and would not assume cardiovascular benefit transfers from subcutaneous to oral formulations[637](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=637)[639](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=639) .
- **The FDA effect-size threshold is applied separately in T2D.** FDA's reading of ATTAIN-2 shows that the ≥5% placebo-adjusted threshold is assessed within the T2D population, where weight loss is smaller[926](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=926)[927](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=927) . This matters for dose selection in programs that enrol obesity with and without diabetes.
- **Generic and hybrid entry has started in the EU.** Liraglutide hybrids referencing Saxenda were authorised in July 2026 via Article 10(3), reflecting the synthetic versus recombinant pro-peptide distinction[604](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=604) .


### Open questions to explore further


Several points could not be resolved from the retrieved records and warrant targeted follow-up. They are the substantive change in the August 2026 FOUNDAYO labeling supplement[663](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=663) , the specific pregnancy PMR for orforglipron[882](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/glp-1-receptor-agonists-in-clinical-development?showSourceNumber=882) , the EU regulatory status and timing for orforglipron, and Phase 3 readouts for retatrutide, CagriSema and maridebart cafraglutide as they reach FDA and EMA filing.
